result.title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels
result.comment: 9 pages (12 pages of appendix & references), submitted to ICLR 2027
result.summary: We study whether \emph{long-horizon model-based value expansion} can serve as an effective framework in pixel-based offline reinforcement learning (RL). Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels is substantially harder than state-based environments, as the agent must learn both the representation and its dynamics, and errors from either can accumulate recursively over imagined trajectories. We introduce MAC-v2, which enables long-horizon model-based expansion from pixels by training a reconstruction-free latent world model with action chunking. By learning representations from prediction and control objectives, MAC-v2 does not need to encode control-irrelevant visual details that can hinder the dynamics prediction. Action chunking further mitigates the prediction error by reducing the number of recursive model predictions required for value expansion. Across diverse visual benchmarks including visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic, and LIBERO-10, MAC-v2 achieves strong performance against model-free and model-based offline RL baselines. Our analyses show that long-horizon model-based value expansion is critical for the performance of MAC-v2, and that both action chunking and latent learning objectives are essential for reliable long-horizon latent imagination.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究像素级离线强化学习中的长时程模型价值展开，提出 MAC-v2：用无重建的 latent 世界模型配合动作分块，从预测与控制目标学习表示，以减少递归想象误差并降低价值展开所需的多步预测次数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「动作分块减少递归 latent 预测次数」与「无重建、面向控制的 latent 表示」可供核查多步 latent 推理中的误差累积与信息坍缩问题，但属机器人 RL 场景，与 VLM 推理的迁移仍需自行判断。
